name: The Forum
text: The square at the middle of Pompeii, 140 metres long, closed to carts. Temples, the basilica, the market and the offices of the town stood round it, and people came to trade, vote and hear the news.

name: Temple of Jupiter
text: The main temple of the town, at the north end of the Forum, built for Jupiter, Juno and Minerva. Vesuvius stands right behind it. An earthquake in AD 62 had already damaged it, and it was still being repaired in AD 79.

name: The Basilica
text: The law court and exchange, on the south-west corner of the Forum, about 150 BC. It is the oldest basilica we know of, and one of the biggest buildings in town.

name: The Stabian Baths
text: The oldest public baths in Pompeii, with a gymnasium, a swimming pool and rooms of different heat. Most citizens went most days, and the stucco ceilings are still there.

name: The Lupanare
text: A small two-floor brothel with ten rooms, the best known of the town’s many. Its stone beds and the pictures and graffiti on its walls are still there.

name: House of the Faun
text: The biggest house in Pompeii, filling a whole block, with two atria and two gardens. A small bronze faun dances in its pool. The huge mosaic of Alexander the Great in battle was found here.

name: The Great Theatre
text: A Greek-style theatre cut into the hillside in the 2nd century BC, for about 5,000 people. The smaller Odeon beside it was roofed, for concerts and readings.

name: The Amphitheatre
text: Built about 70 BC, the oldest stone amphitheatre there is, for some 20,000 people. In AD 59 a fight between the fans of Pompeii and Nuceria here ended in a riot, and Rome shut the arena for ten years.
